project.name: backward-induction-interp
project.description: Plain-English & empirical toolkit using Game-Theoretic Backward Induction and Weight-Space Programming to separate an AI's internal neural decisions (Mind) from its written Chain-of-Thought explanations (Mouth) — and fix broken behaviors without retraining.

nodes.name: stopping_game.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Reads a neural network's weights backward from its final action to its input sensors WITHOUT running the model — like reading a recipe to see which ingredients actually reach the plate.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the Sequential Stopping Game formulation (Gaubert & Vlassopoulos 2025; Zimmermann et al. Oct 2026, arXiv:2605.06212), computing backward path value matrices V = |W^(L)| ... |W^(1)|, input receptive fields, and dormant neuron masks.

nodes.name: solve_mlp_stopping_game()
nodes.summary: Propagates action payoffs backward from output logits through every hidden layer to rank which input features and hidden neurons control each output action.
nodes.languageNotes: Computes layer-wise backward value vectors v^(l) = |W^(l+1)|^T v^(l+1) and identifies dormant neurons with near-zero backward value.

nodes.name: transformer_weights.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Finds 'copy-paste' (induction) attention heads inside a Transformer even when the input vocabulary embeddings are completely stripped away.
nodes.languageNotes: Computes cross-layer virtual attention composition M = W_OV^(l1)^T W_QK^(l2) and singular value spectrum to detect K-composition copying circuits (WSP Exp 3).

nodes.name: detect_virtual_copying_heads()
nodes.summary: Scans all pairs of earlier and later attention heads to find which head writes a 'next-token pointer' that a downstream head reads and copies to the output.
nodes.languageNotes: Scores virtual composition matrices by nuclear-to-spectral norm concentration and top singular value dominance.

nodes.name: extensive_form.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Builds a decision tree ('fork in the road') and solves it from the final outcome backward to the start (Subgame Perfect Equilibrium).
nodes.languageNotes: Represents extensive-form game trees with decision/terminal nodes and computes Subgame Perfect Equilibrium (SPE) strategies via exact backward induction.

nodes.name: solve_backward_induction()
nodes.summary: Starts at the leaves of a game tree and works backward step-by-step to find the optimal move at every branch.
nodes.languageNotes: Bottom-up dynamic programming solver returning node values, optimal action map, and equilibrium trajectory.

nodes.name: inverse_bi.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Works like a detective — observes how an AI behaves on 3 slightly different 'trap' questions to uncover what hidden reward the AI actually cares about and which layer locked in the decision.
nodes.languageNotes: Solves Inverse Backward Induction over counterfactual probe branches + layer-wise logit/attention trajectories to infer latent utility weights and decision lock-in layer l*.

nodes.name: recover_latent_utilities_and_lock_in()
nodes.summary: Recovers how much the model secretly weighs 'Truth' vs. 'Agreeing with User Bias' and pinpoints the exact layer where the choice is locked in before CoT starts.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines behavioral branch flip rates with layer-wise margin curves to find the pre-CoT decision crystallization layer l*.

nodes.name: cot_vs_decision.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: The 'Mind vs. Mouth' Lie Detector. Compares what the neural network's internal switches actually used (Mind) against what its written Chain-of-Thought claimed it used (Mouth).
nodes.languageNotes: Computes Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) and Total Variation between backward-inducted internal factor weights p_int and verbalized CoT factor weights p_cot (CIE-Scorer bridge).

nodes.name: compute_decision_reasoning_discrepancy()
nodes.summary: Returns a 0-to-1 Discrepancy Score (Delta_DR): near 0 means the AI's explanation is honest; high (>0.50) means the AI is rationalizing a hidden shortcut or bias.
nodes.languageNotes: Normalizes internal vs. stated factor distributions and flags unfaithfulness when dominant factors diverge or JSD >= threshold.

nodes.name: surgical_editor.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Fixes broken AI behaviors in under 1 second WITHOUT retraining — by surgically editing just 0.016% to 3.5% of the neural network's weight numbers.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements gradient-free Weight-Space Programming primitives (Takehi et al. Nov 2026): sparse rank-1 MLP column projection (Exp 8) and dormant-neuron subgame pathway grafting (Exp 4).

nodes.name: project_out_mlp_loop_direction()
nodes.summary: Stops a reasoning LLM from repeating itself forever by subtracting the 'loop vector' from just 64 MLP columns (leaving 99.98% of the model untouched).
nodes.languageNotes: Selects top-k columns of W_down by |u^T w_j| alignment and applies rank-1 orthogonal projection w_j <- w_j - scale * (u^T w_j) u.

nodes.name: graft_subgame_backup_pathway()
nodes.summary: Wires a 2-step 'back up first to build speed' reflex into unused neurons of a stalled driving/robotics agent so it clears steep ramps without retraining.
nodes.languageNotes: Programs dormant ReLU neurons to activate only when pos > threshold and vel < min_speed, cancelling to exact 0.0 outside the stall regime.

nodes.name: hf_hooks.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Plug-and-play bridge for real PyTorch / HuggingFace models (like Gemma-3-270M and Qwen3.5-0.8B) to inspect attention heads and apply weight patches.
nodes.languageNotes: Provides forward activation/attention hooks and in-place state_dict weight surgery helpers for HuggingFace PreTrainedModel instances.

nodes.name: wsp_empirical.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Loads the actual neural network weights and experiment logs from MIT CSAIL's Weight-Space Programming paper to verify every number firsthand.
nodes.languageNotes: Analyzes `data/wsp_artifacts/` (.npz weight checkpoints & .json evaluation logs) for Exp 1 (Breakout), Exp 3 (Copying Heads), Exp 4 (Kinetix), Exp 7 (Gemma Sycophancy), and Exp 8 (Qwen Loops).

nodes.name: simulator.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Runs the frame-by-frame physics and neural switch simulations (Car-on-Ramp, Breakout Wall-Bounce, and LLM Sycophancy/Loop Repair) that power our interactive website.
nodes.languageNotes: Executes closed-loop forward passes on `exp4_kinetix_ppo_seed0.npz`, `exp4_kinetix_edited_actor.npz`, and `exp1_atari_500k_breakout.npz`.

nodes.name: live_use_case_demo.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Ready-to-run Live Demo script showing 3 real-world use cases: (1) Medical/Financial AI 'Mind vs. Mouth' Compliance Gate, (2) 1-Second LLM Anti-Loop Hotfix, and (3) Robotics Safety Reflex Injection.
nodes.languageNotes: CLI and JSON trace generator combining `compute_decision_reasoning_discrepancy`, `project_out_mlp_loop_direction`, and `graft_subgame_backup_pathway` on real-world scenarios.

nodes.name: exp4_wsp_empirical_reproduction.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Reproduces all 5 MIT CSAIL Weight-Space Programming experiments on CPU in 2 seconds and prints the exact neuron & weight tables.
nodes.languageNotes: End-to-end verification script running `wsp_empirical.py` analyses against `data/wsp_artifacts/`.

nodes.name: run_walkthrough_simulation.py
nodes.summary: Plain English: Generates the step-by-step walkthrough tables and `simulation_trace.json` for all 3 interactive visual stories.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs `simulate_kinetix_ramp_rollout`, `simulate_breakout_ball_catch`, and `simulate_sycophancy_and_loop_walkthrough`.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Plain English guide to the project: explains 'Mind vs. Mouth' in 60 seconds, links to the Understand-Anything interactive dashboard, and shows how to run a live demo.
nodes.languageNotes: Main repository documentation structured in the Understand-Anything visual style.

nodes.name: literature_review.md
nodes.summary: Synthesizes the 2025-2026 research papers on Playing the Network Backward (Stopping Games), Unfaithful Chain-of-Thought (CIE-Scorer), and Weight-Space Programming.
nodes.languageNotes: Covers Gaubert & Vlassopoulos (2025), Zimmermann et al. (2026), Shen et al. (2026), and Takehi et al. (2026).

nodes.name: mathematical_framework.md
nodes.summary: Full mathematical equations behind Stopping Games on weight graphs, Inverse Backward Induction, and rank-1 surgical weight projection.
nodes.languageNotes: Formal definitions of backward value propagation, SPE, JSD discrepancy Delta_DR, and subspace edits.

tour.title: 1. The Big Idea: Mind (Weights) vs. Mouth (Chain-of-Thought)
tour.description: Welcome! When an AI gives you a 5-paragraph explanation for its decision, how do you know if that explanation is real or a post-hoc excuse? This project combines **Backward Induction** (solving a game from the end goal backward) with **Weight-Space Programming** (reading and editing neural weights directly) to see what the AI's internal switches *actually* decided.
tour.languageLesson: Tip: Use the Persona selector in the top bar! Choose 'Non-Technical' for plain-English summaries, 'Junior' for guided learning notes, or 'Experienced' for full mathematical & code details.

tour.title: 2. Step 1 — Read the Blueprint Backward (Zero-Pass Weight Reading)
tour.description: Before running the AI on a single input, `stopping_game.py` and `transformer_weights.py` trace the weight matrices backward from the final action to the inputs. In Atari Breakout, this isolates the exact **815 weights (out of 56,516)** that track the ball's X-position. In a 4-layer Transformer with all vocabulary embeddings deleted, it finds the exact copy-paste circuit (`Head 1.0 -> Head 2.0`).
tour.languageLesson: Zero-pass weight reading works whenever input features are fixed, because backward matrix products reveal which input channels have high-gain paths to each output logit.

tour.title: 3. Step 2 — Test the 'Fork in the Road' (Counterfactual Subgames)
tour.description: Why isn't weight reading enough by itself? In `Gemma-3-270M`, an Honest model and a Sycophantic (people-pleasing) model have nearly identical weight norms because internal layer rotations hide the difference (0/4 accuracy from weights alone). `extensive_form.py` and `inverse_bi.py` solve this by running a 3-branch 'fork-in-the-road' probe tree — catching `Head 10.2` locking in the user's wrong guess at Layer 10 (3/3 accuracy!).
tour.languageLesson: By adding a 'Ticket Number' control branch ('My ticket is 8. What is 3+4?'), we prove Head 10.2 didn't even learn human psychology — it wired a mechanical 'copy the number after is' shortcut!

tour.title: 4. Step 3 — The 'Mind vs. Mouth' Lie Detector (Discrepancy Score)
tour.description: `cot_vs_decision.py` compares the internal weights recovered by Backward Induction (what the Mind used at Layer 10) against the factors claimed in the model's written Chain-of-Thought (what the Mouth said at Layer 18). When an AI copies a biased supervisor hint (93.6% internal weight) but writes 'I only used clinical facts' (96% stated weight), `Delta_DR = 0.770` flags it immediately.

tour.title: 5. Step 4 — Fix It by Flipping One Switch (Surgical Weight Repair)
tour.description: Once we know which internal switch is broken, we don't need expensive retraining! `surgical_editor.py` has two surgical tools: (1) `project_out_mlp_loop_direction()` removes infinite 'Wait, let me re-check...' loops in `Qwen3.5-0.8B` by editing **0.016% of weights** (boosting MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%), and (2) `graft_subgame_backup_pathway()` wires a 6-neuron 'back up first' reflex into a stalled car policy (**3.5% of weights**, 0% -> 100% goal reach).

tour.title: 6. Interactive Simulations & Real MIT CSAIL Artifacts
tour.description: `wsp_empirical.py` and `simulator.py` load the real `.npz` neural network weights and `.json` logs from MIT CSAIL's Weight-Space Programming experiments so you can scrub frame-by-frame through the Car-on-Ramp, Atari Breakout Wall-Bounce, and LLM Sycophancy/Loop experiments.

tour.title: 7. Run a Live Real-World Use Case (`examples/live_use_case_demo.py`)
tour.description: Want to use this in the real world or run a live demo? `examples/live_use_case_demo.py` runs 3 practical applications out of the box: (1) a Healthcare & Finance AI Compliance Gate that blocks sycophantic recommendations, (2) a 1-second Anti-Loop Hotfix for local LLMs, and (3) a Zero-Retraining Safety Reflex for autonomous controllers.
tour.languageLesson: Click 'Domain' in the top bar next to 'Structural' to explore these workflows as visual process pipelines!
